A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Splat Feature Solver. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, feature-reconstruction, runtime, ablation and rendering-weight experiments, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds camera-pose corruption results and comparisons of feature-lifting fidelity.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same row-sum solver, opacity guidance, clustering and mask filtering, and automatic threshold selection. v2 expands the aggregation implementation description but does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: LeRF-OVS, 3D-OVS and the existing feature and kernel coverage remain. v2 adds a distinct input-condition scenario: feature lifting with corrupted camera poses on the existing LeRF scenes.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 introduces direct comparisons against Semantic Gaussian and Argmax Lifting across seven feature types, supplemented by Figures 13–14. These methods were discussed but not evaluated in v1's feature-fidelity comparison. Existing segmentation and runtime comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new pose experiment fixes geometry trained with clean poses and corrupts selected images using Gaussian rotation noise with a one-degree standard deviation and translation noise scaled by scene size/100. It varies corruption rates and evaluates mIoU. This is an additional protocol, not a documented revision of the retained benchmark settings.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix C adds a systematic robustness study covering seven nonzero pose-corruption rates and a clean control, with quantitative results in Table 3 and qualitative comparisons in Figure 9. This tests a new failure source beyond v1's retained component ablations, opacity sensitivity and mask-noise examples.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced. The existing per-pixel weight-sum means and standard deviations are retained in renumbered tables. Gaussian noise parameters specify perturbations, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Headline segmentation, runtime and existing ablation scores remain unchanged. New Table 3 reports mean mIoU of 65.0, 60.8 and 28.1 at 20%, 50% and 100% pose corruption. Table 9 adds baseline scores; for SAM+OpenCLIP, Semantic Gaussian and Argmax Lifting obtain 83.2 and 83.4 mean cosine similarity, versus the retained 90.4 for the proposed method.

T1.justification: The linear formulation, Jensen surrogate, beta approximation argument and background-opacity derivation are retained. Equations are consolidated and renumbered, and v1 Appendix F becomes v2 Appendix G. No substantive proof or formal assumption is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The principal contributions and abstract/conclusion claims remain. However, the introduction strengthens its generality positioning: v1 says many existing methods specialize in particular features or kernels, whereas v2 says all aforementioned methods exclusively focus on SAM+CLIP features and 3DGS kernels.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains pose robustness through rejection of misaligned masks and discusses eligibility for feature-fidelity comparisons. Appendix H also describes the solver as optimal under any convex loss, a stronger interpretation than the retained approximation-bound argument supports. Existing discussion and limitations otherwise largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the 75% mask-overlap threshold and clarifies cluster-level feature assignment, configuration reuse and instructions for opening packaged supplementary material. These are documentation additions rather than established procedure changes. The explicit cuML implementation identifier for HDBSCAN in v1 is omitted.

R1.justification: The bibliography and three-family taxonomy remain. v2 expands positioning against feature-agnostic alternatives and explains exclusions of DrSplat and grouping methods, replacing v1's blanket figure-caption rationale that other methods require feature compression. Its introduction also more categorically restricts prior methods' scope.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the overall narrative remain. Focused revisions expand the framework overview, qualitative discussion and two appendix sections, while adding numbered subsections and a multimedia appendix. This is localized rewriting rather than a wholesale narrative revision.

P2.justification: v2 changes the two-column format to a single-column layout, consolidates five main tables into two multipart tables, revises diagrams and captions, relocates existing figures, and adds robustness and baseline-comparison displays. The revised Figure 12 also mismatches image/feature labels in its ViT and MaskCLIP panels.

improvement.justification: Direct feature-fidelity comparisons and the controlled pose-corruption study strengthen empirical support beyond v1, while added aggregation details improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by reporting problems: Table 3's clean Ramen/Teatime values conflict with Tables 1(a) and 4, Figure 12 mislabels panels, and Appendix H overstates the unchanged approximation result as optimality. The net improvement is useful but limited.
